title: Mid‐Holocene Seasonal and Annual South American Temperatures Across PMIP Phases: Contrasts With Modern Climate and Evaluation Against Proxy Records
content:
Abstract

This paper describes seasonal and annual Mid-Holocene (MH) temperature in South America simulated by PMIP2, PMIP3, and PMIP4 experiments and compares with information extracted from paleoclimate proxies. The study is focused on seasonal and annual MH anomalies with respect to the pre-Industrial (PI) climatology in PMIP2, PMIP3, and PMIP4 as well as MH anomalies with respect to the present-day (PD) climate in PMIP3 and PMIP4 (PD was not part of PMIP2 experiments). Results show that the three PMIP generation of models agree on colder MH in austral autumn and warmer MH in austral spring with respect to the PI which is a consequence of insolation changes. With the inclusion of modern warming produced by anthropogenic forcing, PMIP3 and PMIP4 agree on colder MH with respect to the PD except over broad areas in austral spring in which the reduction of temperature from MH to PI in response to insolation changes has not been reversed by human-induced warming yet. Comparisons of these model results against proxy-based reconstructions is challenging over most of South America due to three main reasons: (a) proxy information is scarce or absent over broad areas; (b) there are marked discrepancies among paleorecords extracted from nearby sites; and (c) estimated proxy uncertainties imply wide ranges of values of the reconstructed anomalies. Comparisons between paleorecords and model outputs over areas with unequivocal proxy-based signals of change show dissimilar results.
